content: The coadministration of fexinidazole with other drugs can lead to significant pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions, primarily due to its inhibition of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This inhibition can result in increased plasma concentrations of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, thereby elevating the risk of adverse effects. Additionally, fexinidazole may prolong the QTc interval, which can further exacerbate the risk of cardiotoxicity when combined with other QT-prolonging agents. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Fexinidazole and Arformoterol/Fexinidazole and Fexinidazole-Aripiprazole: Both combinations increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely for QT prolongation. 2. Fexinidazole and Potassium Channel Blockers: Avoid coadministration with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval due to the risk of severe QT prolongation. 3. Fexinidazole and Armodafinil: Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Fexinidazole and Arsenic Trioxide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 5. Fexinidazole and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both combinations increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Fexinidazole also increases the levels of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4. 6. Fexinidazole and Asenapine/Asenapine Transdermal: Both combinations increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 7. Fexinidazole and Atazanavir: Atazanavir decreases the levels of fexinidazole, while fexinidazole increases the levels of atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Fexinidazole and Atenolol/Betaxolol/Bisoprolol: These combinations may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of bradycardia. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 9. Fexinidazole and Atogepant: Fexinidazole increases the levels of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Fexinidazole and Atomoxetine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Fexinidazole and Atorvastatin: Fexinidazole increases the levels of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Fexinidazole and Avanafil/Avapritinib/Avatrombopag: Fexinidazole increases the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Fexinidazole and Axicabtagene Ciloleucel/Brexucabtagene Autoleucel: These combinations may increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Fexinidazole and Axitinib: Fexinidazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Fexinidazole and Azithromycin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Fexinidazole and Bedaquiline: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, and fexinidazole increases the levels of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Fexinidazole and Belumosudil: Fexinidazole increases the levels of belumosudil by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Fexinidazole and Belzutifan: Belzutifan decreases the levels of fexinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Fexinidazole and Bendamustine: Fexinidazole increases the levels of bendamustine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Fexinidazole and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Fexinidazole increases the levels of this combination by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Fexinidazole and Benzphetamine: Fexinidazole increases the levels of benzphetamine by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Fexinidazole and Bromocriptine: Fexinidazole increases the levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Fexinidazole and Budesonide: Fexinidazole increases the levels of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Fexinidazole and Buprenorphine (Various Forms): Fexinidazole increases the levels of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4, and both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Fexinidazole and Bupropion: Fexinidazole decreases the levels of bupropion by inducing CYP2B6. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Fexinidazole and Buspirone: Fexinidazole increases the levels of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Fexinidazole and Busulfan: Fexinidazole increases the levels of busulfan by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Fexinidazole and Butabarbital/Butalbital: These drugs increase the levels of fexinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Fexinidazole and Cabozantinib: Fexinidazole increases the levels of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Fexinidazole and Caffeine: Fexinidazole increases the levels of caffeine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Fexinidazole and Calcifediol/Calcitriol: Fexinidazole increases the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Fexinidazole and Capecitabine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Fexinidazole and Capivasertib: Fexinidazole increases the levels of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4. Modify therapy and monitor closely. In summary, fexinidazole's inhibition of CYP3A4 and its potential to prolong the QTc interval necessitate careful consideration of drug interactions. Avoid coadministration with drugs that share these risks, and monitor closely when alternative therapies are not feasible.
